To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have performed the ﬁrst lattice QCD study on ﬂuctuations in (2+ 1)-ﬂav orQCD at nonzero density.
we have calculated the baryon number and strangeness fluctuations and correlations at zero and nonzero chemical potential for (2+1) ﬂavor QCD on the lattice.
the baryon-strangeness correlations show a peak at nonzero chemical potential and that the baryonic ﬂuctuations show a peak as well, when they are analyzed in an expansion up 1 to sixth order.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of hadronic fluctuations and correlation s in the vicinity of a possible quark-hadron phase transition.
the study of the phase transition of the strong interaction, the so-called QCD phase transition.
the properties of hadrons in the medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are consistent with a smooth crossover, but that there is no clear evidence of a ﬁrst order phase transition.
the lattice data are in agreement with the predictions of the chiral quark model.
, at the present level of knowledge, the data are not yet conclusive enough to decide between the various scenarios.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Taylor expansion of the pressure in the chemicalequilibrium is a very powerful tool to investigate the QCD phase structure at nonzero chemicalpotentials.
we have shown how to calculate the Taylor coefficients at nonzero chemical potential and how they behave with increasing order.
the Taylor series expansion is a good tool to study the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Taylor expansion is a useful tool to extract the ﬂuctuations of conserved charges from lattice data.
the peak in the higher order cumulants is not a ﬁctitiousartifact due to the truncation of the Taylor expansion.
the Taylor expansion is not a good approximation to the free energy in the low temperature region.
